title: Transport of a supplied local subscheme morphism to the open slice site

source.place: Sheaves Tag 00A0 (3), Lemma 6.31.1, open-subspace restriction and canonical identification of stalks, including module sheaves. Read https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00A0 on 2026-10-13.

statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U an open containing x, and F,N module sheaves on the slice over U [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write E for the slice/open-subscheme equivalence and T for the module stalk at x on U. Given a T(E(F))-to-T(E(N)) linear map q, an open A of U containing x, and an actual morphism f:E(F)|_A -> E(N)|_A whose germ on every section near x agrees with q, there exist x in V contained in U, a natural restriction-stalk comparison a:R_VU S_V ≅ S_U [def-sc-open-module-stalk-functor], and k:R_VU(F) -> R_VU(N) with S_V(k)=a_F followed by the restriction of scalars of q along U.ι.stalkMap followed by a_N inverse. This is solely transport of the supplied f; no local existence of f or finite freeness is asserted.

proof.text: Set V=U.ι image A. Copy the base map of U.ι.isoImage A so its value at the marked point is definitionally the marked point of V. Restriction along this isomorphism is an equivalence, with unit and counit obtained from Modules.restrictFunctorComp, restrictFunctorCongr and restrictFunctorId. Compose it with Modules.overEquiv V to obtain the fully faithful functor D from slice sheaves on V to module sheaves on A. Modules.overMapCompOverEquiv and the equality e.hom followed by homOfLE(V≤U)=A.ι give b:R D ≅ E_U restrict A. Define k as D.preimage of b_F followed by f followed by b_N inverse. Use the proved restrictionStalkLinearNatIso helper of OpenModuleStalkRestrictionComparison for e.hom and A.ι. The equality e.hom followed by V.ι=A.ι followed by U.ι identifies the two composite stalk ring maps. Whisker the two linear comparisons, b and restrictScalarsComp/restrictScalarsCongr to obtain a. Its formula, naturality of the comparison, D.map_preimage and the restriction-stalk germ formula show that conjugating S(k) by a sends each germ of a section over B in A to the germ of f.app B on that section. This entire construction is the proved private exists_slice_hom_with_subscheme_germ_formula helper; it contains no remaining obligations.

Cancel the component a_N from the desired equality and compare the underlying functions on a stalk element m. The additive isomorphism Modules.restrictStalkNatIso A.ι supplies a preimage of a_F(m) on the stalk of the restriction to A. Presheaf.exists_germ_eq represents that preimage by a section s over an open B containing the marked point of A. Modules.germ_restrictStalkNatIso_hom_app identifies its image with the germ of s on A.ι image B. Apply the private transport helper germ formula and the supplied equation hf B hxB s, then cancel a_F inverse followed by a_F. This proves the requested equation after restriction of scalars without changing any hypotheses.

proof_origin.place: Sheaves Lemma 6.31.1, Tag 00A0 (2)-(3), including modules; formal transport via Mathlib natural isomorphisms and the existing proved linear restriction-stalk comparison, followed by germ representation and the supplied hf.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_open_stalk_hom_of_subscheme_lift
    (X : Scheme.{u}) (U : X.Opens) (x : X) (hxU : x ∈ U)
    (F N : SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over U))
    (q : (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace ⟨x, hxU⟩).obj
        ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj F) ⟶
      (RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor U.toScheme.toRingedSpace ⟨x, hxU⟩).obj
        ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj N))
    (A : U.toScheme.Opens) (hxA : (⟨x, hxU⟩ : U.toScheme) ∈ A)
    (f : (Modules.restrictFunctor A.ι).obj ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj F) ⟶
      (Modules.restrictFunctor A.ι).obj ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj N))
    (hf : ∀ (B : A.toScheme.Opens)
      (hxB : (⟨⟨x, hxU⟩, hxA⟩ : A.toScheme) ∈ B)
      (m : Γ((Modules.restrictFunctor A.ι).obj ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj F), B)),
      ((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj N).presheaf.germ (A.ι ''ᵁ B) ⟨x, hxU⟩
          ⟨⟨⟨x, hxU⟩, hxA⟩, hxB, rfl⟩ (Modules.Hom.app f B m) =
        q (((Modules.overEquiv U).functor.obj F).presheaf.germ (A.ι ''ᵁ B) ⟨x, hxU⟩
          ⟨⟨⟨x, hxU⟩, hxA⟩, hxB, rfl⟩ m)) :
    ∃ (V : X.Opens) (hxV : x ∈ V) (hVU : V ≤ U),
      let R := SheafOfModules.overMap.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (homOfLE hVU)
      let S := openModuleStalkFunctor X V ⟨x, hxV⟩
      ∃ (a : R ⋙ S ≅ openModuleStalkFunctor X U ⟨x, hxU⟩)
        (k : R.obj F ⟶ R.obj N),
        S.map k = a.hom.app F ≫
          (ModuleCat.restrictScalars (U.ι.stalkMap ⟨x, hxU⟩).hom).map q ≫
            a.inv.app N

from.place: Only the slice/open-subscheme transport step, after the local morphism has already been supplied.

mathlib_searches.query: Transport a morphism of module sheaves on an open subscheme through the equivalence with the slice site, preserving its map on stalks
mathlib_searches.results: Eight hits, principally Tilde restrictions and Scheme.Modules.Hom.app; no theorem combining the slice transport and the supplied germ equation.
The natural isomorphism overMapCompOverEquiv is available and is used in the proof plan; it does not itself provide the transported stalk equation.
Mathlib Modules.Sheaf has overMapCompOverEquiv and germ formulas. Searches in lean/Sheaf and lean/WeilConjectures found individual transport uses, not this supplied-morphism transport theorem.
